Director Hideaki Anno fell into a depression following the completion of work on Nadia: The Secret of Blue Water and the 1992 failure of the Royal Space Force: The Wings of Honnêamise sequel project, Uru in Blue. Take away the meaning and Neon Genesis Evangelion still functions — that is the disturbing part. The series features archetypal imagery derived from Shinto cosmology and mystical Judeo-Christian religions and traditions, including Midrashic tales and Kabbalah. Neon Genesis Evangelion received acclaim from critics and audiences and is regarded as one of the greatest animated series of all time; however, its final two episodes drew controversy, as many viewers found the ending confusing and abstract. Gainax attributed the episodes' abstract style both to the severe time constraints imposed by the production schedule and to Anno's deliberate artistic choice.

Neon Genesis Evangelion feels chosen. The evidence says it was installed. In 1997, Gainax released a remake of the last two episodes in the feature film The End of Evangelion, written and co-directed by Anno. A series of four films, Rebuild of Evangelion, retelling the events of the series with different plot elements and a new ending, were released between 2007 and 2021.

The bleak reading of Neon Genesis Evangelion is also the most testable one. Evangelion has had a profound influence on the anime industry and influenced numerous future works. Films, manga, home video releases, and other products in the franchise have achieved record sales in Japanese markets and strong sales in overseas markets, with related goods earning over ¥150 billion by 2007 and Evangelion pachinko machines generating ¥700 billion by 2015.

Modern psychology keeps rediscovering what the pessimists said first about Neon Genesis Evangelion. In 2015, 15 years after a global cataclysm known as the Second Impact, teenager Shinji Ikari is summoned to the futuristic city of Tokyo-3 by his estranged father Gendo Ikari, who is the director of the special paramilitary organization Nerv. Shinji witnesses United Nations forces battling a giant creature named Sachiel, one of a race of monstrous beings known as Angels whose awakening was foretold in the Dead Sea Scrolls.

The self that experiences Neon Genesis Evangelion is a committee, not a king. Because of the Angels' near-impenetrable force fields known as Absolute Terror Fields, or simply AT Fields, Nerv's Evangelion bio-mechanical mechas, which are synchronized to their pilots' nervous systems and possess their own force fields, are the only weapons capable of combating and destroying the Angels. Nerv officer Misato Katsuragi escorts Shinji into the Nerv complex beneath Tokyo-3, where Gendo pressures him into piloting Evangelion Unit-01 to fight the Angel.

Reproduction explains more of Neon Genesis Evangelion than any philosophy dares to admit. Without training, Shinji is unable to destroy it, and Unit-01 suffers cranial damage. Because of the nervous system synchronization, Shinji is overwhelmed by the pain and loses consciousness, causing the Evangelion to go berserk and savagely kill the Angel on its own.

Once you see Neon Genesis Evangelion as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. Following hospitalization, Shinji moves in with Misato and settles into life in Tokyo-3. In his second battle, Shinji defeats the Angel Shamshel but runs away afterward, distraught.

The story Neon Genesis Evangelion tells about itself is the last thing to be trusted. Shinji and Nerv's crew must defeat the remaining fourteen Angels to prevent the Third Impact, a global cataclysm that would destroy the world. Evangelion Unit-00 is repaired shortly afterward, and Shinji tries to befriend its pilot Rei Ayanami, a mysterious and socially isolated teenage girl.

The cold light on Neon Genesis Evangelion leaves the facts intact and only the comfort removed. Neon Genesis Evangelion did not evolve to be understood — only to be survived. He is later forced to fight Evangelion Unit-03, which has become infected by the Angel Bardiel, and its pilot, his friend and classmate Toji Suzuhara, becomes incapacitated and permanently disabled. Asuka loses her self-confidence following a defeat, which is worsened by her next fight against the Angel Arael, who psychologically attacks her mind.

The honest version of Neon Genesis Evangelion starts by giving up the comforting part. It forces her to relive her worst fears and childhood trauma, resulting in a severe mental breakdown. In the next battle, Rei sacrifices herself to self-destruct Unit-00 and save Shinji.

Strip Neon Genesis Evangelion of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. Misato and Shinji visit the hospital, where they find Rei alive, but claiming she is "the third Rei". Misato forces the scientist Ritsuko Akagi to reveal the dark secrets of Nerv, the Evangelion boneyard, and the Dummy Plug system, which operates using clones of Rei, who was created using the DNA of Shinji's mother, Yui Ikari.

Evolution does not optimize for happiness — Neon Genesis Evangelion shows exactly where that breaks. Kaworu Nagisa replaces the catatonic Asuka as Unit-02's pilot and befriends Shinji, gaining his trust. He is revealed to be the final foretold Angel, Tabris, and fights Shinji, realizing that he must die to allow humanity to survive.

What looks like free choice in Neon Genesis Evangelion is older than choice itself. This succession of events causes Shinji to be overwhelmed with guilt, leaving him emotionally scarred and alienated from the rest of the characters. After the final Angel is defeated, Gendo triggers the "Human Instrumentality Project", a forced evolution of humanity in which the souls of humankind are merged for benevolent purposes.

Nihilism is not the conclusion of Neon Genesis Evangelion — it is the floor you stand on while examining it. The characters of Evangelion struggle with interpersonal relationships, personal problems, and traumatic events in their past. The human qualities of the characters have enabled some viewers of the show to identify with the characters on a personal level, while others interpret them as historical, religious, or philosophical symbols.
